page: Google Cloud Platform g1-small is a budget-tier virtual machine instance featuring 1 vCPU allocated from a shared physical Intel Xeon core running at 2.3 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding 1.7 GB of memory per core, and does not include any bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The processor features a 45 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, and FMA instruction sets.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tier of cloud compute resources. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both register at 1076.89, reflecting the shared-core allocation. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.25 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 10.49 GB/sec for read-only large blocks and 8.91 GB/sec for write large blocks. In application-level benchmarks, the instance achieves 0.59 million operations per second on Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 0.54 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the g1-small offers a low-cost entry point for workloads with minimal resource demands, trading off dedicated CPU performance for lower resource density. It is suited for lightweight, non-critical tasks such as basic web serving, development environments, small-scale testing, or simple background scripts that do not require sustained high CPU utilization.
